data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The preference is indefensible on Popper's own terms because any reason to prefer a corroborated theory for future action necessarily assumes the uniformity of nature, thereby smuggling in the very induction Popper sought to eliminate.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If one can act without expectation, the preference is mere randomness.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the preference is based on anything other than past success, it is not a preference for the 'better-corroborated' theory.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Logical collapse: demonstrating that 'acting on' implies 'expecting success,' which implies 'assigning higher probability,' contradicting the core tenet that corroboration is not probability.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
